subject: Reasoning
description: Direction sense — N/S/E/W movement, compass turns, distance and final position calculation, shortest path.

questions.stem: Ravi walks 10 m North, then 5 m East, then 10 m South. How far is he from his starting point?

options.option_text: 0 m back to start point (option here)

questions.explanation: TRACK each move on a coordinate system. Start at (0,0). Move 10m N → (0, 10). Move 5m E → (5, 10). Move 10m S → (5, 0). Distance from origin = √(5² + 0²) = 5m. Direction: directly EAST. KEY INSIGHT: the 10m N + 10m S CANCEL OUT (net 0 in y-direction); only the 5m E remains. METHOD: sum NORTH-SOUTH moves (signed, N+ S−) and EAST-WEST moves (E+ W−) separately. Final position = (E_total − W_total, N_total − S_total). Distance from start = √(x² + y²) (Pythagoras if non-zero in both axes). EXAMPLES — practice: (1) 4N, 3E → distance √(9+16) = 5m NE. (2) 6E, 8N, 6W → 8N (6E and 6W cancel) — distance 8m N. (3) 5N, 12E, 5S, 12W → back to origin (0m). EXAM TRAP: students forget to assign SIGNS; or confuse 'distance walked' (sum of all moves) with 'displacement' (straight-line from start). DISTANCE = path length; DISPLACEMENT = vector. PYQ FREQUENCY: direction sense problems are SSC CGL Tier 1, IBPS Clerk Pre, RRB NTPC favorites — 1-2 per paper.

questions.stem: A man walks 15 m N, turns RIGHT and walks 10 m, turns RIGHT again and walks 15 m. He is now facing:
questions.explanation: Track facing direction at each turn. Start facing N (walking North). RIGHT TURN → now facing E (walks 10 m E). RIGHT TURN again → now facing S (walks 15 m S). So final facing direction is SOUTH. CARDINAL DIRECTION TURNS: from any direction, RIGHT TURN goes 90° clockwise: N→E→S→W→N. LEFT TURN goes 90° counter-clockwise: N→W→S→E→N. ABOUT-FACE (180°): N↔S, E↔W. POSITION TRACKING: Start at (0,0). After 15m N: (0, 15). After 10m E: (10, 15). After 15m S: (10, 0). So final position is 10 m due EAST of starting point — distance 10m, in eastern direction. EXAM TIP: when problems mix turn-direction with facing-direction, draw a quick diagram with the man's position + arrow showing his facing direction at each step. SHORTCUT: even number of right (or left) turns may bring back to original direction; odd number of turns gives perpendicular direction. PYQ FREQUENCY: turning direction Qs in SSC CGL Tier 1, IBPS Clerk Pre — 1× per paper.

questions.stem: Ankit moves 6 km East, then 8 km North. The shortest distance from the starting point is:
questions.explanation: Apply PYTHAGORAS theorem. Two legs are 6 km (E) and 8 km (N) — perpendicular to each other. Shortest distance (hypotenuse) = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 km. KEY INSIGHT: 6-8-10 is a SCALED 3-4-5 PYTHAGOREAN TRIPLE (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25 are common). Recognize and skip calculator. SAMPLE OTHER PRACTICE: (1) 5 km E, 12 km N → distance √(25+144) = √169 = 13 km. (2) 9 km W, 12 km S → √(81+144) = √225 = 15 km (3-4-5 scaled by 3). DIRECTION OF SHORTEST DISTANCE: the diagonal connecting start to end — would be at angle θ from East, where tan θ = 8/6 = 4/3 → θ ≈ 53° (north of east). KEY METHOD for direction problems: (1) plot moves on coordinate axes. (2) use Pythagoras for shortest distance. (3) trigonometry for angle if asked. INSIGHT: 'shortest distance' = straight-line displacement = different from total path walked (in this question 6+8=14 km is total path). PYQ FREQUENCY: 6-8-10 / 5-12-13 problems in SSC CGL, IBPS Clerk, RRB NTPC — 1-2× per paper.

questions.stem: Standing in the morning, your shadow is to your LEFT. Which direction are you facing?
questions.explanation: MORNING: sun is in the EAST (rises in east). Your shadow always falls AWAY from the sun. So if shadow is to your LEFT, sun must be to your RIGHT → if right is EAST, then you are facing NORTH. KEY METHOD for direction-by-shadow problems: (1) Identify TIME OF DAY: morning (sun east), evening (sun west), noon (sun nearly overhead, weak shadow). (2) Identify SHADOW DIRECTION: opposite of sun. (3) Reason about facing direction. EXAMPLES: (a) Morning, shadow to your RIGHT → sun is to LEFT (east) → facing SOUTH. (b) Evening, shadow to your LEFT → sun to right (west) → facing SOUTH. (c) Evening, shadow to your RIGHT → sun to left (west) → facing NORTH. (d) Morning, shadow in front → sun behind → facing WEST. (e) Evening, shadow behind → sun in front → facing WEST. AT NOON, sun is approximately OVERHEAD (in tropics) — shadow nearly vanishes; in N. Hemisphere mid-latitudes (like North India), noon sun is to the SOUTH; shadow to the NORTH. ASTRONOMY: Earth rotates W to E → sun appears to move E to W; equator gets sun overhead at equinoxes. PYQ FREQUENCY: shadow-direction problems in SSC CGL Tier 1, IBPS Clerk Pre — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: A person walks 4 m N, 3 m E, 2 m S, 6 m W. His final position from start is:
questions.explanation: Track moves: Start (0,0). +4 N → (0, 4). +3 E → (3, 4). +2 S → (3, 2). +6 W → (−3, 2). Final position: (−3, 2) — i.e., 3 m WEST and 2 m NORTH of starting point. Distance from start: √(3² + 2²) = √(9+4) = √13 ≈ 3.6 m. Direction: NORTH-WEST quadrant. NORTH-OF-WEST angle: tan θ = 2/3 (north over west) → θ ≈ 33.7° N of W. KEY METHOD: separate into NS and EW components; net N = 4 − 2 = 2 m N; net E = 3 − 6 = −3 m (i.e., 3 m W). Position: 2N + 3W. Distance: √(2²+3²) = √13. EXAM TIP: in MCQ context, 3.6 m NW is approximate; sometimes options give √13 m or 3.6 m NW or various phrasings. PRACTICE — when net x and net y are both non-zero: result is in a DIAGONAL direction (NE, NW, SE, SW). When one is zero, result is purely cardinal (N, S, E, W). PYQ FREQUENCY: complex direction problems with multiple legs in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO Mains, RRB Group D 1× per paper.

questions.stem: Anil is standing facing East. He turns 135° clockwise, then 180° anti-clockwise. He is now facing:
questions.explanation: Track angle. Start facing EAST (0° in standard math, or 'right' direction). Turn 135° CLOCKWISE: 90° clockwise from E = S; another 45° clockwise = SW. So after 135° CW: facing SW. Then 180° ANTI-CLOCKWISE from SW: SW + 180° = NE. Hmm, that gives NE not NW. Let me recompute. Method: assign each direction a degree (0°=N, 90°=E, 180°=S, 270°=W, going clockwise). Start facing E = 90°. CW 135° → 90° + 135° = 225° = SW. ACW 180° → 225° − 180° = 45° = NE. So final = NE. The given correct option (NW) doesn't match. Possibly the question intended different angles; or the correct option is mislabeled. UNDER STRICT compass-degree interpretation: answer = NE. In any case, KEY METHOD: track angle on COMPASS (each cardinal at 90° apart, intermediate at 45°: NE=45°, SE=135°, SW=225°, NW=315°). Apply turns by adding (CW) or subtracting (ACW) angle. NORMALIZE final angle to 0-360° range. EXAM-FAVORITE: 90°, 135°, 180°, 270° turns; 360° = full circle (back to original). PYQ FREQUENCY: angular-direction problems in IBPS PO, SBI PO Mains 1-2× per paper.

questions.stem: Ravi walks 5 m N, 3 m W, 5 m S, 7 m W. He is now in which direction from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Track: Start (0,0). 5m N → (0, 5). 3m W → (−3, 5). 5m S → (−3, 0). 7m W → (−10, 0). Final: 10 m due WEST of starting point (no N-S component). KEY: the 5m N + 5m S CANCEL OUT (no net y-displacement); the 3m W + 7m W ADD to 10m W. So position is 10m W of start, no N or S. DIRECTION = pure WEST. INSIGHT: for direction-sense problems, ALWAYS check if any moves cancel. PRACTICE: similar problems where N and S cancel, leaving pure E/W; OR where E and W cancel, leaving pure N/S. EXAM TIP: when computing direction, check if ONE of the (x, y) components is ZERO — then direction is purely cardinal. If BOTH non-zero, direction is diagonal (NE, NW, SE, SW); if both zero, the person is at start. SHORT-CUT FOR EXAM: don't bother computing distances for direction-only Qs — just track signs. PYQ FREQUENCY: cardinal-only-direction problems in SSC CGL, IBPS Clerk Pre — 1× per paper.
